title: Law Lets I.R.S. Seize Accounts on Suspicion, No Crime Required
author: Shaila Dewan
bias_or_interest: Mainstream investigative journalism; independent of the parties. Primary evidence of its own front-page headline.
relevant_locations: Front-page article, 2014-10-25 (print 2014-10-26); headline text; Carole Hinders / Mrs. Lady's restaurant facts; $32,820.56 seizure; IRS-CI policy-change statement (Richard Weber)
quotation_note: Headline is directly quotable (grade-A): 'Law Lets I.R.S. Seize Accounts on Suspicion, No Crime Required.' Hinders' own statements (mother's habit, unaware banks reported deposits) are self-reported and must stay indirect/hedged.
rights_note: Quote the headline as reported fact; do not reproduce full article text. Secondary reporting used for corroboration, not as sole basis for legal conclusions.
notes: Anchor source for the NYT front-page beat (CLM-0007), seizure facts (CLM-0002), person facts (CLM-0001), and the IRS-CI policy signal (CLM-0008). fact_recheck: exact print date (Oct 25 online / Oct 26 print) and IRS memo ordering vs. front page (memo ~2014-10-17).

title: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 — Structuring transactions to evade reporting requirement prohibited
organization: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School (U.S. Code text)
relevant_locations: 31 U.S.C. § 5324(a) — prohibition on structuring transactions to evade the currency transaction report requirement
quotation_note: Statute makes it an offense to structure, assist in structuring, or attempt to structure a transaction for the purpose of evading the reporting requirements of section 5313(a).
notes: Primary statutory basis for the structuring offense (CLM-0004) and its legislative placement (CLM-0015). Added by the Money Laundering Control Act of 1986.

title: 31 U.S.C. § 5313 & 31 C.F.R. § 1010.311 — Currency transaction reports over $10,000
organization: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School (U.S. Code / C.F.R.)
relevant_locations: 31 U.S.C. § 5313(a) and 31 C.F.R. § 1010.311 — financial institutions must file a report (CTR) for currency transactions exceeding $10,000; obligation falls on the institution
quotation_note: The reporting duty is the bank's; a single CTR is filed for cash transactions over $10,000.
notes: Primary basis for the $10,000 reporting-threshold beat (CLM-0003). The obligation is on the bank, not the depositor — central to the myth-correction.
